name: cd
description: Changes the current working directory of the shell.

flags.description: Switch to the previous directory (equivalent to cd "$OLDPWD").
Move up one level to the parent directory.
Move to your home directory; ~user moves to another user's home.

examples.explanation: Moves to the /etc/nginx directory using an absolute path (starting from the root /).
Moves into a relative path, resolved from the current directory.
Moves up one level to the parent directory.
Prints the previous directory after switching to it, making it easy to toggle between two locations.
With no argument, cd goes to your home directory ($HOME).

about: cd is a shell builtin, not an external program, because a child process cannot change the working directory of its parent shell. The shell tracks the current directory in the $PWD and $OLDPWD variables.
Absolute paths start with / and are resolved from the filesystem root; relative paths are resolved from your current location.
useCases: Navigate the filesystem during daily work.
Jump between two directories quickly using cd -.
mistakes: Using cd with a path containing spaces without quotes: cd My Documents fails; use cd "My Documents".
Expecting cd to persist after a script exits — scripts run in their own shell.
warnings: None significant; cd cannot delete or modify anything.
